name: @growth-lab/gl-charts
description: The Growth Lab data-visualization spec as a themed layer over TanStack Charts v0.

scripts.check: npm run tokens:check && npm run typecheck && npm run test

comments.peerDependencies: TanStack Charts is pre-alpha and has shipped API changes in PATCH releases, so the peers are pinned exactly rather than caret-ranged. Bumping them is a deliberate act: re-run `npm run reference` and diff the render before accepting a new version.
comments.exports: Ships TypeScript source, matching this repo's convention of sourceable assets over build artifacts. Your bundler compiles it. TanStack itself ships built ESM + .d.ts, so it needs no special handling.
comments.devDependencies: The TanStack devDeps are pinned to the same exact versions as the peers. A caret range would let the gallery render against a version the package does not claim to support, which is precisely the drift `npm run gallery` exists to catch.
comments.check: The three cheap gates, in the order that fails fastest: tokens:check catches a hand-edit of a generated file, typecheck catches the API, test runs tests/*.test.ts (bundled through esbuild by scripts/run-tests.mjs, because the package ships TypeScript source and has no build step). `npm run gallery` is the expensive gate and stays separate — it needs Chrome and the fonts.
comments.tokens: Every design value is authored once in tokens.json and emitted into src/tokens.ts and src/tokens.css. tokens:check re-emits into memory and fails if either file drifts from the source; tokens:downstream reports (never fails on) the repo's other hand-carried token copies listed in README.md's propagation table.
comments.dependencies: Five d3 LAYOUT packages, and the shape of the rule is the same for all five: TanStack Charts ships marks and transforms but no layout of any kind (marks are rect/bar/line/dot/area/arrow/hexagon/link/rule/text/tick; transforms are bin/stack/group/normalize/rank/reduce/window/cumulative). Where a chart needs geometry computed before any mark exists, the geometry has to come from somewhere, and d3 is where it comes from — TanStack's own treemap catalog entry reaches for d3-hierarchy too (see reference/tanstack-treemap.md). d3-hierarchy owns the treemap, sunburst, nested donut and tidy tree; d3-sankey the flow diagram; d3-force the network; d3-delaunay the triangulation and its Voronoi dual; d3-contour the iso-lines. Every one is a REAL dependency, declared and pinned exactly, never a transitive one — none is in TanStack's dependency tree, and src/shapes/geo.ts explains at length why this package never imports a d3 specifier it has not declared. They are pinned rather than caret-ranged because a layout change moves every mark on the chart, so a minor bump is a deliberate act: re-run `npm run gallery` and diff the render before accepting one. d3-geo is the deliberate exception and stays UNDECLARED: a projection is an editorial choice the caller makes, so the geo entry takes a factory as an argument and derives its types from TanStack's descriptor.
comments.docs: The primitives reference (docs/) is the third question the package answers about itself: the gallery asks whether a chart type can be drawn on-spec, the examples page whether it survives real data, and this one what each exported primitive actually IS. It draws no chart — the mark swatches are 120x32 glyphs stroked from `glDefaults(kind, {})` called at build time, not TanStack renders — and every word on it is extracted: signatures and prose from `src/**` through the TypeScript compiler API, the mark defaults table by CALLING the library and probing each property with a sentinel to measure pinned-vs-overridable, token values from tokens.json. `docs:check` fails on a module that parsed to nothing (a rename, or a parser regression, would silently drop a whole section) and on any external reference, and REPORTS documentation coverage rather than failing on it — the two-line `gl*` wrappers are deliberately doc-free, and a gate that failed on them could only ever be satisfied with filler prose.
comments.examples: The examples page (examples/) is the gallery's counterpart: the gallery proves each chart type can be drawn on-spec from synthetic data shaped to be awkward, and the examples page proves the same types survive contact with a real dataset that was not designed to flatter them. `examples` bundles it to ONE self-contained HTML — fonts, data and code inlined — so it can be handed to someone who does not have this repo. `examples:check` mounts that file in Chrome and fails if any demo did not draw, lost its source panel, or lost its source line. `examples:data` re-pulls the committed Atlas snapshots and is the only script that needs the 11 GB release mounted (set ATLAS_HOME); everything else builds from the JSON in examples/data/. It is deliberately NOT part of `check` — it needs the network and a local Atlas release, which no CI gate should assume.
comments.dependencySize: The four layout packages added for the catalog work are small and dependency-light: d3-contour and d3-sankey pull d3-array (and d3-shape for sankey), d3-force pulls d3-dispatch/d3-quadtree/d3-timer, d3-delaunay pulls delaunator. They are only reachable through @growth-lab/gl-charts/shapes, which is a separate entry point precisely so a consumer who never draws a network never pays for one.
